searchText: can someone help me understand how blob rate-limiting works at the EL right now? i only see a per-transaction limit but i thought we wanted a hard cap per-block within the execution layer nothing is stopping me right now from making a block with say 10 transactions with 4 blobs each there separately happens to be a hard cap at the CL but i figured if anything the EL should be driving this and the CL should just verify hmm looks like this is specified here: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/6583 happy to work w/ <@415548822983278593> to get this merged unless someone feels the current state of things is fine <adietrichs> > <adietrichs> There are several small things like that that the PR clarifies, so probably a good idea to get it up to date & merged (re @sharded_data_bot: <ralexstokes> hmm looks like this is specified here: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/6583 happy to work w/ @ansgar.eth to get this merged unless someone feels the current state of things is fine) <adietrichs> My understanding is that all client implementations are already correct though, so this is about bringing the EIP itself in line with that. not sure what changed but the EIP used to specify a maximum number of blob commitments per block. i think that got dropped while we were trying to decide on allowing 0 blobs in this txn type or not either way, the cleanest thing to me is that we just have some amount of per-block data gas (that determines a per-block cap) and everything else flow through that if client mempools have per-txn limits that is up to them Does this imply you could create a transaction with more blobs than the block data gas limit? If so, then it's on clients to deal with that in their mempool however they see fit? That _seems_ best, given we'll likely raise the blob count in the future, and so you can imagine previously invalid txns becoming valid once that happens? the EIP gives a hard cap per-txn, but not per-block if anything we should have a per-block limit and clients should be free to have a per-txn limit but that can be a local policy for their mempool

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
can someone help me understand how blob rate-limiting works at the EL right now?

i only see a per-transaction limit but i thought we wanted a hard cap per-block within the execution layer

nothing is stopping me right now from making a block with say 10 transactions with 4 blobs each

there separately happens to be a hard cap at the CL but i figured if anything the EL should be driving this and the CL should just verify

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
hmm looks like this is specified here: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/6583

happy to work w/ <@415548822983278593> to get this merged unless someone feels the current state of things is fine

excerpts.content: not sure what changed but the EIP used to specify a maximum number of blob commitments per block.

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
i think that got dropped while we were trying to decide on allowing 0 blobs in this txn type or not

either way, the cleanest thing to me is that we just have some amount of per-block data gas (that determines a per-block cap) and everything else flow through that

if client mempools have per-txn limits that is up to them

excerpts.content:

That _seems_ best, given we'll likely raise the blob count in the future, and so you can imagine previously invalid txns becoming valid once that happens?
